extracted.intended_audience: investor relations professionals and corporate communications teams at public companies
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for IR teams on producing effective investor-facing communications across channels (website, presentations, annual reports, earnings calls, media, and social). Focuses on content, format, process, legal/compliance considerations, and channel-specific best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make a Strong First Impression with Your Website
rubrics_metrics.description: A company’s investor relations website is often the first place that potential investors and financial analysts will go; it can serve as an indispensable marketing tool and means of information delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide any information needed by investors and financial analysts for decision making so it is readily available; the investment community values transparency and more information is better. Outline the investment thesis on the opening page to highlight strategic vision, initiatives and key performance indicators. Include interactive graphs to communicate financial performance, current and archived annual reports, press releases, regulatory filings, webcasts, corporate governance and contact information. Consider technology features (information download managers, email alerts, podcasts). Ensure the site is easy to navigate, mobile friendly and organized for quick information retrieval. Example: BP’s website and its interactive IR tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop Effective Investor Presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Create presentations that clearly articulate why the company is a worthwhile investment without overloading the audience with information that clouds the investment thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use market intelligence to determine critical investor information. Within the first few minutes provide a quick snapshot of the investment opportunity: market opportunities, company positioning, and strategy for growing revenue, earnings and cash flow over mid- to long-term. Limit historical results to key financial and operating measures to establish a track record. End by reiterating key investment messages. Keep total presentation length to no more than 20–25 minutes. Example: Encompass Health’s investor presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a High-Quality Annual Report
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report conveys company performance and progress, fulfills regulatory requirements, and can act as a marketing tool to attract investors; it should balance comprehensiveness with concision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical key sections: key financial highlights and strategic initiatives, letter to shareholders, Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A), financial statements, auditor’s report, corporate governance. The letter to shareholders and MD&A are most important: the letter presents CEO/chair overview of performance and outlook; MD&A explains key factors driving performance (industry trends, market risks, acquisitions/divestitures, R&D, competing products). Use management insights and investor feedback to develop a core theme introduced in the cover and letter and reiterated with supporting information. Start early: develop a timeline with stage deadlines, responsibilities, and allow time for review and approval by senior management, the board, legal counsel and others. Example: RPM International’s annual report theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct an Informative Earnings Conference Call
rubrics_metrics.description: Earnings calls should elaborate on the earnings release to help investors and analysts forecast future performance and to link results to long-term strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure should be consistent with the earnings release. Calls are typically quarterly and should explain financial and operating results relative to strategy and initiatives to avoid overreactions. Develop a script to ensure clarity and reduce misinterpretation. Typical duration 45 minutes to an hour, with prepared remarks no more than 20 minutes. Webcast presentations and make recordings/slides available on the IR website. Consult legal counsel about archive duration for compliance. Rehearse delivery, anticipate Q&A, and gather investor/analyst feedback before and after the call to improve future calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate Media Relations into Your Investor Relations Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage business and financial press to enhance visibility and deliver the investment story to large audiences; media coverage can serve as credible third‑party endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop relationships with targeted reporters and editors by providing compelling story ideas consistently and by being a subject-matter expert on industry topics. Begin outreach with smaller outlets (trade publications, local media, newswires like Bloomberg, Dow Jones, Reuters) and expand to mainstream press once the investment story is clear—recognize the competition for coverage. Use thorough planning, preparation, media training and rehearsals for spokespeople. Example: Apple coverage illustrating strategic direction under leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Social Media as an Alternative Information Source
rubrics_metrics.description: Investors and analysts increasingly use social media, blogs and message boards to gather information, which can surface market-moving news earlier than traditional channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have training, publishing protocols and regulation-compliant approval procedures in place; consult legal counsel because disclosure regulations vary by country and exchange. Use social media to supplement legally compliant disclosure channels only after information has cleared the market and is public, or to augment marketing/ thought leadership (e.g., investor blogs). Monitor conversations—especially from influencers—and use monitoring tools (e.g., StockTwits). Example: eBay used a GIF to deliver IR highlights on Twitter. Be cautious because social media missteps can backfire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set Appropriate Expectations and Be Candid
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications should present opportunities while also candidly disclosing challenges; doing so builds credibility and trust with the investment community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair candid discussion of challenges with thorough, easily accessible information to establish credibility. Setting appropriate expectations helps avoid investor overreaction and supports long-term trust. This principle applies across website content, presentations, annual reports, calls, media interactions and social media.
